one_liner: RocksDB's built-in Ribbon SST filter: same FP rate as its Bloom filter in about 30% less memory, at 3-4x CPU.
what_it_does: A static set-membership filter with no false negatives and a configurable FP rate. RocksDB builds one per SST file (or filter partition) in place of its Bloom filter. You enable it with NewRibbonFilterPolicy(bloom_equivalent_bits_per_key, bloom_before_level) on BlockBasedTableOptions::filter_policy, the C functions rocksdb_filterpolicy_create_ribbon/_hybrid, or the config string "ribbonfilter:N". You give the Bloom bits/key you used before, and it targets the same FP rate with fewer bits (9.9 gives 1% FP in about 7 bits/key instead of 9.9).
how_it_is_fast: The win is space, not speed. Ribbon (Rapid Incremental Boolean Banding ON-the-fly) is a perfect-hash static function over GF(2). Each key hashes to a start column and a 128-bit coefficient row, which approximates a band matrix (Dietzfelbinger-Walzer). The system is solved by on-the-fly Gaussian elimination that behaves like linear-probing hash insertion, followed by back-substitution. A query computes the parity of an r-bit window in an 'interleaved' column-major solution that spans 1-3 adjacent cache lines. The XOR construction avoids Bloom's roughly 1.44-1.5x space factor. Splitting between b-1 and b solution columns gives fractional bits/key.
when_to_use: RocksDB databases where SST filters stay resident in RAM for a long time (defaults, or cache_index_and_filter_blocks with optimize_filters_for_hits) and filter blocks take a large share of block cache; the blog's example LOG shows 14% of a 9 GB cache.

Leveled or universal LSMs with long-lived lower levels. Use the hybrid (bloom_before_level=N) so flushes and L0 get Bloom and deeper levels get Ribbon. The blog's cost model puts the break-even at about 1 hour of filter lifetime.
FP rates around 1-10%. Standard Ribbon w=128 is 6-8% over the information-theoretic minimum there, against about 50% for blocked Bloom.
Roughly 10K-10M keys per filter, the range r=128 is tuned for. The blog says even 100M keys in one filter save 27% vs Bloom.
Outside RocksDB: a static key set known up front, when you want portable C++ with fractional bits/key and are willing to vendor util/ribbon_*.h the way pdillinger/fastfilter_cpp did.
when_not_to_use: Short-lived filters (flush/L0 output, data living under about an hour) or write-bound workloads. Construction costs 3-8x Bloom CPU, and the wiki warns it 'could slow peak write rates in some cases.'

CPU-bound point lookups on memory-resident data. Paper Table 2 has queries at 58 vs 10 ns/key (n=10^6) and 140 vs 36 ns/key (n=10^8) against RocksDB's FastLocalBloom, and Ribbon queries get relatively costlier at low FP rates.
Sets that grow after build. Ribbon is static, and RocksDB's memtable filter stays Bloom.

Compaction hosts that are tight on memory and build huge unpartitioned filters. Construction needs about 230 bits/key of temporary memory vs about 75 for Bloom: 3 GB vs 1 GB for 100M keys in one filter, untracked unless cache charging is enabled.
Partitioned filters over cold data without optimize_filters_for_hits, where only some filters are resident; the blog says the benefit is 'not as clear' there.

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (built into RocksDB); standalone use is a source-drop of the templated util/ribbon_alg.h + ribbon_impl.h headers
integration.dependencies: Inside RocksDB: RocksDB itself (compression libs and gflags optional). Standalone: a handful of RocksDB support headers (math128.h, fastrange.h, port.h, etc.; the fastfilter_cpp fork ships coding_lean.h, fastrange.h, lang.h, math.h, math128.h, port.h)
integration.min_toolchain: Current RocksDB: C++20, GCC >= 11 or Clang >= 10 (INSTALL.md; CMake defaults to C++20). The Ribbon headers themselves say they are written for C++11, and the 2021 paper copy built with GCC 8.4.1.
integration.platforms: Any platform RocksDB supports (Linux, macOS, Windows VS2017+, AIX, BSDs per INSTALL.md). The Ribbon code uses no processor intrinsics, only compiler built-ins for prefetch, clz/ctz and parity, with native 128-bit ints when available and a fallback otherwise. Open issue #14065: an upcoming MSVC flags a potential divide-by-zero (C4723) in ribbon_impl.h, which fails warnings-as-errors builds.
integration.thread_safety: Managed by RocksDB. Each SST's filter builder has a single owner; only EstimateEntriesAdded() is documented as thread-safe (for parallel compression). Thread safety of the standalone ribbon_*.h classes is not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — inside RocksDB it is a one-line swap of NewBloomFilterPolicy(bpk) for NewRibbonFilterPolicy(bpk) at the same FP rate, and either policy reads both filter kinds (RocksDB >= 6.15). It covers only static SST filters, and as a standalone structure it is not a Bloom replacement: there is no incremental insert and all keys must be known before build.

gotchas: Default bloom_before_level=0 still writes Bloom filters for memtable flushes under leveled and universal compaction, so savings only appear as compaction rewrites files. Use -1 for all-Ribbon. Since 8.7 the option can be changed at runtime through SetOptions.

It silently falls back to Bloom, with only an info-log warning, when a filter has more than 950M keys, when a small filter (<1024 slots) would be smaller as Bloom, after 256 failed re-seeds, or when cache charging for the banding memory hits the limit.

Temporary construction memory is untracked by default. Enable block-cache charging for filter construction (reserve_table_builder_memory in 6.27, now cache_usage_options / CacheEntryRole::kFilterConstruction), or use partitioned filters or smaller SSTs.
Downgrading to RocksDB < 6.15 reads Ribbon filters as 'no filter' until compaction rebuilds them. RocksJava has only a BloomFilter class and no dedicated Ribbon class.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over BuRR, which gets below 1% overhead with bumped Ribbon but is research code, and over xor/binary fuse (xor_singleheader: faster queries, about 13-23% overhead, single header), when you already run RocksDB or want a production-hardened C++ Ribbon with Bloom-like fractional bits/key. Choose BuRR for minimum space and xor/binary fuse for the fastest static-filter queries; ribbonGo is the Go option.
verified_claims_summary: arXiv:2103.02515 Table 2 used a 2021 copy of RocksDB's ribbon code in the fastfilter_cpp fork (Xeon D-2191 Skylake DE, GCC 8.4.1 -O3 -march=skylake-avx512, FP rate about 1%). Standard Ribbon w=128 had 6-8% space overhead vs 49.8% for RocksDB's FastLocalBloom, but cost 166 vs 21 ns/key to build and 58 vs 10 ns/key to query at n=10^6, and 235 vs 72 and 140 vs 36 ns/key at n=10^8. The RocksDB blog's filter_bench figures (no hardware stated) are 7 vs 10 bits/key, 140 vs 32 ns/key to construct and 600 vs 500 ns/key to query; no std:: baseline applies.
status_note: RocksDB is actively maintained (last push 2026-09-25). The Ribbon code itself is stable: the headers have only had reformat/modernize commits since 2024 and filter_policy.cc last changed in Nov 2025. It has been production-ready since 6.22, its SST schema has been long-term supported since 6.20, and it is dual GPLv2/Apache-2.0, so the headers can be vendored.
